final_draft.answer: No. As of 16 November 2026, our GitHub organisation (harborlight) does not require two-factor sign-in for its members.
final_draft.note: Needs review before sending: the approved answer and the live setting disagree. The approved answer (answer:8fe2d083-f23d-46a7-b328-52313003987a, owner security@harborlight.example, CC6.1, valid until 2027-11-16) says the harborlight GitHub organisation requires two-factor sign-in for all members. A live check on 2026-11-16T17:10:37Z (evidence:9ab308c6-0ab9-461c-a3f3-a14da873d96d) found that it does not. I wrote the draft from the live result so we don't send a claim we know is false. Before this goes out: (1) Ask the answer owner to turn on required two-factor sign-in in the GitHub organisation, or confirm why it is off. (2) If it is turned on, run the check again and update the answer to 'Yes'. (3) Fix or retire the approved answer so it stops giving the wrong answer. Separately, the Access Control Policy (section 4.2) and the approved employee MFA answer say all workforce members must use a second factor through the identity provider. That is about employee accounts, not GitHub sign-in settings, so I didn't use it here. Do not use it to imply GitHub requires two-factor sign-in.
